title: riverside-payments-integration-call-notes-2026-05-12
content:
Call notes: Riverside Payments integration kick-off (quick sketch, rough).

Date: 2026-05-12
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood CS), Samir Rao (Redwood Solutions), Jenna Liu (Account Exec),
  - Riverside: Priya Menon (CTO), Mark Ellison (Lead Engineer), Claire Zhou (PM)

Objective: Understand Riverside's primary use case (real-time txn enrichment + fraud signal augmentation) and surface immediate blockers for Redwood hosted API + Dedicated option evaluation.

Background/context (from prior emails): Riverside processes ~1.2M transactions/day, peak 10k RPS burst windows. They need low-latency enrichment (<=50ms target per request ideally for internal routing) and strong PII controls. Considering Redwood Hosted API for PoC, but enterprise security wants Dedicated or Private for production.

Key asks from Riverside:
  - Proof-of-concept to enrich transactions with 1-2 model calls (entity extraction + risk-score)
  - Data residency: EU region required for a subset of customers
  - SLA: 99.9% uptime for production; can accept lower for PoC
  - Cost target: need run-rate estimate (cost per 1M tokens + embeddings) and Dedicated pricing ballpark for their volume

Technical details discussed:
  - Payload: JSON with transaction metadata, customer id, merchant id, textual notes (avg 120 tokens), sometimes attachments (merchant notes).
  - Expected model: start with small open model (Llama-2-70B(.chat) quantized) for entity extraction and a tuned reranker for fraud heuristics. They currently evaluate embeddings for deduping and similarity (embedding sizes 1536).
  - Latency sensitivity: synchronous call in their routing path. We discussed options: prefix caching + hot KV cache for repeat merchants, and Dedicated with lower tail latency.
  - Security: must support VPC peering + KMS-managed keys for logs and optional on-prem connector for restricted data flows.

Gotchas / Risks noted:
  - Their peak bursts (10k RPS) imply batching could be beneficial but batching introduces extra latency; need to simulate their request distribution (Samir to request sample traces).
  - Attachments: they may want to send short text snippets; clarify max payload sizes and whether they will send base64 attachments (ASK: Mark to confirm typical attachment size).
  - Compliance: some EU customers require that raw text never leave their VPC — Private deployment likely required for those. Need legal to confirm acceptable audit logs.
  - Cost expectations vs reality: they assume cheaper per-token than typical; must prepare explicit unit economics and recommend quantization + model distillation options.

Action items / Next steps (owners & rough ETA):
  1) Run initial perf estimate: Samir to run back-of-envelope Dedicated capacity and per-token cost for 1.2M/day + burst pattern (ETA 2026-05-15).
  2) Request traffic trace/sample: Asha to send email to Mark asking for anonymized 24h sample traces (no PII) to simulate latency/batching (ETA 2026-05-14).
  3) Security checklist: Jenna to loop in security (private-deployments lead) and start scoping VPC/KMS requirements; include note about audit log retention (ETA 2026-05-18).
  4) PoC plan draft: Asha + Samir to produce 1-page PoC plan (scope, success metrics, infra choices hosted vs dedicated, timeline). Share with Riverside by 2026-05-17.
  5) Pricing ballpark: Finance to provide Dedicated monthly commit estimate; Jenna to coordinate (ETA 2026-05-16).
  6) Jira tickets: create initial epic JIRA-RIV-73 and break out technical tasks (Asha).

Open questions (to resolve on next call):
  - Which EU region(s) are required exactly? (Ireland vs Frankfurt?)
  - Do they require explicit on-prem deployment, or will VPC + Private control plane suffice?
  - Will they accept eventual consistency for enrichment (async) for lower cost, or must be strictly synchronous?
  - What is acceptable PII redaction process for PoC data?

Notes to self:
  - Follow up to push for a small synthetic trace if they are hesitant to share real logs.
  - Prepare two PoC paths: (A) Hosted API with strict VPC/KMS and allowed network egress restrictions, (B) Dedicated private deployment. Highlight tradeoffs in latency/cost/ops.
  - Save sample perf numbers from recent Dedicated case study (Confluence-4821) to cite.

Meeting vibes: positive, pragmatic. Riverside cares about predictability and compliance more than bleeding-edge model accuracy. They are open to phased approach (hosted PoC -> Dedicated for EU customers).

Reference links/ids to attach to Jira: CONFLUENCE-4821 (Dedicated case study), JIRA-RIV-73 (epic), GH PR (placeholder) https://github.com/redwood-inference/riv-poc-template (ask eng to create repo stub).

Short-term tasks (this week): get sample trace + perf estimate + 1-page PoC. Prioritize security scoping for EU data.

-- end of notes --

Informal: will flesh into a proper PoC doc next after we get traces. Throwing this in Drive so Jenna/ Samir can edit.
